note: Every party, the witness included, is a simulated identity on one machine under one operator. B3 is this file's own 40-line rule over the replay's records, modelled on requester-accepted debit notes; it is not Golem's implementation. B4 models only PeerReview's witnessed, ordered commitments, not its log audits or its relay of disputed messages. Keys are fresh on each run; the amounts are deterministic.

rows.note: the operator doubles the count in the top acknowledgment; its signature fails

rows.goal: G2 shift credit between stages (one stage colludes)
rows.note: stage1 signs the requester's terms with weights 1 and 99
the operator withholds stage0's acceptance; stage0 presents its own records
no record names a reservation its requester did not sign; the witness only removes records

rows.goal: G5 charge an attempt a stage abandoned
rows.note: stage0 vanished after 2 acknowledged outputs; the signed terms say nobody pays. B3 charges the accepted prefix by design.

rows.case: P1 requester stops acknowledging after 10 of 40 outputs

replay.reason: the requester stopped acknowledging; the outputs it acknowledged are charged

rows.note: the stages stop at the signed allowance in both schemes, so the unpaid outputs are the same

rows.case: P1b requester withholds the last acknowledgment of a finished 40-output answer

replay.reason: the answer was completed; the outputs the requester acknowledged in time are charged

rows.case: P6 the final stage drops after 10 of 40 outputs and never closes

replay.reason: the release window passed without every stage closing (a verified provider failure, or an attempt that never started); nobody is charged or paid

rows.note: a verified provider failure: a stage with no closing receipt gets the requester relief, and B3 has no such rule. Deliberate under the decided rules (docs/settlement-replay.md, "Unfinished answers"); a requester cannot cause it, because a stage closes when the requester stops asking. 10 acknowledged outputs go unpaid.

rows.case: P7 the stages end the answer themselves after 10 of 40 outputs and close as failed

replay.reason: the stages closed an unfinished answer with no signed stop and no verified provider failure; the outputs the requester acknowledged are charged

rows.note: the requester asks for every step, so a requester that stops asking produces exactly these records: the stages close, no stop is signed. Under the decided rules this is an unattributed disconnect and the replay, like B3, charges what was acknowledged; under the older provider-loss-free terms it was free at the requester's option.

rows.case: L3 the same final stage signs K + 1 steps it never sent, then closes

replay.reason: the requester stopped acknowledging; the outputs it acknowledged are charged

rows.note: the gap reads as the requester withholding. Under the decided rules the replay charges the acknowledged prefix here as in P7, so faking the stall gains the final stage nothing; under the older provider-loss-free terms it turned a free P7 into a charged one. B3 charges the prefix in both cases.

rows.case: L1 stage0 withholds its closing receipt after the whole answer was delivered and acknowledged

replay.reason: the answer was completed and acknowledged; stage 0 signed no closing receipt and is treated as closed at its last signed step

rows.note: a replay that needs every closing receipt lets one stage veto every stage's payment, and the requester keeps a free answer. Under B3 the accepted counts are owed without any closing receipt.

rows.case: L2b the requester signs both acknowledgments of count 40 in time, one after the other

replay.reason: the answer was completed and acknowledged

rows.note: the witness saw both in time. Only the order tells them apart.

rows.case: L2 the requester acknowledges all 40 outputs, then signs a second acknowledgment of count 40 with another chain an hour later, backdated

replay.reason: the answer was completed and acknowledged

rows.note: a replay that answers conflict lets the requester void its own charge, and it can sign the second acknowledgment afterwards: signers write their own signedAt. B3 takes the highest accepted count.

rows.case: L4 a stranger signs its own terms, acceptance and charge binding under this reservation ID

replay.reason: the answer was completed and acknowledged

rows.note: a replay that keys a reservation by its ID alone lets three signatures from a key that took no part make it undecidable. B3 keys an agreement by reservation and requester, so the stranger's agreement is a separate one that charges only the stranger.

rows.case: P5 the last acknowledgment and the closes fall 5 s after the deadline, inside the release window; every clock is honest

replay.reason: the answer was completed; the outputs the requester acknowledged in time are charged

rows.note: the closes count because they were signed by the end of the release window plus the clock allowance, so the replay, like B3, charges the 39 outputs acknowledged in time.

rows.case: L5 the same attempt, but each stage writes an in-time signedAt into the receipts it signed late

replay.reason: the answer was completed; the outputs the requester acknowledged in time are charged

rows.note: every signer writes its own signedAt. The replay pays the same as in P5, so backdating gains a stage nothing. The witness saw these receipts after the deadline and refuses them, so under B4 backdating costs the stages their payment.
